turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Come through, Mrs Naidoo. Shame, the queue was long today, load shedding threw the whole clinic out.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, I'm tired and irritable, I'll say it. I came for this knee and the work form, not a lecture.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Easy, love. Doctor, I'm her husband, I brought her. The bakkie's parked on a meter, so we can't be long.
[SEG0004] person_4 (DOCTOR): Knee. Which side?
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): Right. Um, two weeks... well, actually closer to three. Aches on the stairs at the office.
[SEG0006] person_4 (DOCTOR): Swelling?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): No swelling.
[SEG0008] person_4 (DOCTOR): Give way or lock?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): No. It doesn't give way and it doesn't lock. Can we move?
[SEG0010] person_4 (DOCTOR): Pain tablets?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Panado, two tablets when it aches. Maybe once a day. Not every day.
[SEG0012] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She forgets half the time, if I'm honest.
[SEG0013] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any blood pressure tablets?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): I stopped it in March. The water tablet, hydrochlorothiazide, twelve and a half milligrams. It had me up all night peeing and I couldn't work.
[SEG0015] person_4 (DOCTOR): Nothing since March?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Nothing. And I'm not going back on it.
[SEG0017] person_1 (NURSE): Doctor, sorry to jump in. Her first pressure was one sixty-eight over ninety-eight.
[SEG0018] person_4 (DOCTOR): That's high. We'll start amlodipine five milligrams daily today.
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): We will not. It's white coat. It always shoots up in this room. I'm not taking a new tablet.
[SEG0020] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She does get anxious in clinics, hey. And her father had a stroke, just so you know, he was about sixty-four.
[SEG0021] person_1 (NURSE): I did repeat it. After she sat quietly it was one fifty-four over ninety-two. Pulse seventy-six, regular.
[SEG0022] person_4 (DOCTOR): Chest pain?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0024] person_4 (DOCTOR): Headache? Short of breath?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): No headache, no, I'm not short of breath. I just want the knee sorted and that form.
[SEG0026] person_4 (DOCTOR): Alright. With that lower repeat, scratch the amlodipine. No tablets started today.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Good.
[SEG0028] person_4 (DOCTOR): Home readings instead. Sister will issue a monitor. Morning and evening for two weeks, write them all down.
[SEG0029] person_1 (NURSE): Ja, I'll fetch the cuff from the cupboard just now and show her.
[SEG0030] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She stays with me. I'll make sure the mornings get written down.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag, don't fuss. I'll do it. I just don't want pills.
[SEG0032] person_4 (DOCTOR): Come back in two weeks with the book. Then we decide. Not before.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Fine. And the form? My supervisor wants it for light duty.
[SEG0034] person_4 (DOCTOR): I'll sign light duties for one week. No heavy stairs if you can help it.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): The lift is broken half the time, so that's a joke, but okay.
[SEG0036] person_4 (DOCTOR): Let me look. Any operation on this knee before?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Never.
[SEG0038] person_4 (DOCTOR): Bend. No heat, no swelling, full bend. Tender on the inner side.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Eina. Ja, that's it. It's not that bad, I'm just over this day.
[SEG0040] person_4 (DOCTOR): Mild strain on the inner side. Nothing broken about it. Carry on with the Panado as you have been.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): So you're not saying I've got high blood pressure?
[SEG0042] person_4 (DOCTOR): Not off today. It may be white coat. Two clinic numbers aren't a diagnosis.
[SEG0043] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): But with her dad's stroke, shouldn't she just take the tablet?
[SEG0044] person_4 (DOCTOR): No. Not today. Home numbers first. If they're fine, we leave it.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): See? I told you.
[SEG0046] person_1 (NURSE): The machine's the Omron one, upper arm. I'll set it before you go out.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): Will it hurt? I'm not in the mood.
[SEG0048] person_1 (NURSE): It just squeezes. Same as what I did.
[SEG0049] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any other medicines I should know about? Diabetes, cholesterol?
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing else. I don't have those.
[SEG0051] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She drinks coffee all day, doctor, that's all. And she was cross about the parking, ignore that.
[SEG0052] person_4 (DOCTOR): Coffee's not my problem today. Form gets signed here. Monitor from sister. Back in two weeks.
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): Can I go? I've got to fetch the grandkids after this and I'm finished.
[SEG0054] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll get the bakkie. Thanks, doctor. Hey, don't forget the book.
[SEG0055] person_4 (DOCTOR): Off you go.

spec.situation: Patient attends for something minor (a knee or a form) and the nurse finds high BP; BP read aloud twice with different numbers; patient says it is white coat; family history of stroke said in passing; no tablets started today, home monitoring arranged.
features: doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.

omissions.text: Hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg was stopped in March because it caused nocturia/'up all night peeing' and interfered with work.
Amlodipine 5 mg daily was initially proposed for high blood pressure, but the patient refused it and the doctor then cancelled it; no blood pressure tablets were started today.
The repeat blood pressure was taken after she sat quietly.
Pulse 76 bpm was regular on the repeat set of observations.

The husband questioned whether she should take the blood pressure tablet because of her father's stroke history, and the doctor explicitly disagreed, saying no tablet today and to use home readings first.
Follow-up instruction was to come back in two weeks with the written home blood pressure record/book, and not before.
The home blood pressure monitor specified was an Omron upper-arm machine, and the nurse would set it up and show her how to use it.
Doctor stated 'Nothing broken about it' regarding the knee.
